subject: Bluebell: intermittent timeouts and long-tail completions — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Michael Santos <michael.santos@bluebell.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Intermittent timeouts & rising errors on /generate - seeing long tails

Rishi,

We started seeing a pattern yesterday evening where our checkout personalization calls to /generate intermittently time out and a growing fraction of requests return 500s. P95/P99 look fine most of the time, but over the past 6 hours a subset of traffic has completed after many seconds/minutes (10s->60s). Our ops team is flagging it as a P1 because it correlates with failed checkouts.

What we observe:
- Burst around 21:15 UTC with a long tail of completions stretching to 45s
- Error rate spiking to ~3.2% for the affected route
- Throughput steady but queue depth on our side increased (we're retrying a few times)

Can you help triage? We can provide traces and a sample of failing request payloads.

--
Michael Santos
Head of Engineering, Bluebell Retail
michael.santos@bluebell.com

Michael — thanks for the heads up and the detail. Sorry you're hitting this.

We're treating this as an escalation. I've looped in Laura (runtime), Hannah (SRE), and Marissa (CS/exec). Please attach the traces and one representative payload; the trace link you mentioned to the Drive would be perfect.

2) We'll pull p95/p99/queue depth and token distribution for the last 6 hours.
3) If we confirm capacity-driven tail, we'll apply a short-lived drain/route split to a lower-concurrency variant to protect user-facing traffic.

I'll keep you posted in this thread.

Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts & rising errors on /generate - seeing long tails

Folks — initial findings from trace sampling (attached trace-sample-20270518.json):
- Multiple worker processes hit configured concurrency_cap (64) repeatedly during the 21:10–21:30 window.
- When cap is reached, requests are queued on the scheduler and show increased queue_time (~1–30s).
- A subset of requests then experience slow KV cache reads (redis p99 elevated), compounding the latency to >40s.
- No immediate kernel-level crashes or OOMs; CPU/GPU utilization stayed in expected range.

Hypothesis: transient spike in prefix-heavy requests plus a hot-shard in KV cache caused head-of-line blocking and queue growth. Concurrency cap prevented new workers from spinning up (safety policy).

Suggested mitigations (short horizon):
- Increase concurrency_cap to 96 for affected pool and enable a controlled burst window (10m) to clear backlog.
- Warm the KV shard (preheat) for the top 10 keys observed in the traces.
- Apply a fallback route for Bluebell traffic to our lower-cost variant with larger concurrency and ok-quality settings while we stabilize.

I'll kick off the cap bump in staging then mirror to production with Hannah's signoff.

-Laura
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intermittent timeouts & rising errors on /generate - seeing long tails

Confirmed from SRE dashboards:
- The scheduler for bluebell-prod-pool shows sustained queue depth > 250 during the spike window.
- Autoscale did not trigger additional nodes because the policy blocks scale-up when concurrency_cap is reached (we've hit a policy blind spot).
- Error types are ~75% upstream timeouts (gateway) + 20% application 5xx (kv timeouts).

Immediate action taken (11:05):
- Increased pool concurrency cap to 96 (rolling update across nodes) — observing gradual queue drain.
- Temporarily enabled a 10-minute traffic split to bluebell-fallback variant (lower quality but higher throughput).
- Notified Bluebell ops (Michael) and asked them to pause aggressive client retries for 30 minutes while backlog clears.

I'll monitor telemetry; if we see re-accumulation we'll revert changes and open a longer outage window for controlled work.

-Hannah
SRE Lead
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Subject: Bluebell executive summary and follow-ups — long-tail surge on 2027-05-18

Michael / Rajiv — summary for your CTO: 

What happened:
- On 2027-05-18 21:10–21:30 UTC Bluebell's traffic included a concentration of prefix-heavy personalization requests that produced long token-generation tails. Several serving workers reached their configured concurrency cap. When the cap was hit, requests queued in the scheduler where slow KV cache reads (redis shard hotness) further delayed processing, producing long-tail completions and a small number of 5xx.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Raised concurrency_cap from 64 -> 96 for the affected pool and performed a rolling update to drain backlog.
- Enabled a temporary traffic split to a fallback variant to protect checkout latency.
- Prewarmed top KV keys and patched autoscale policy to allow scale-up when queue depth exceeds 200 even if concurrency_cap was previously hit.

Impact:
- Peak error rate: 3.2% (affected route).
- Post-mitigation: error rate reduced to ~0.6% within 15 minutes; queue depth returned to baseline within 25 minutes.

Next steps / recommended follow-ups:
1) We will run a 2-week observation window and provide a postmort with token distribution heatmaps and recommendations for Bluebell-specific capacity profiles.
2) Option: commit to a short burst reservation for Black Friday-style peaks (pre-authorized cap increases + warm cache) — we can model cost impact.
3) Engineering change: update the autoscaler rules to consider queue depth as a hard signal and add a finer-grained KV replication for hot keys (medium-term).

I'll assign owners and calendar a 30-minute review tomorrow to walk through the traces and the cost model (invite to follow). Apologies for the disruption; we'll follow through until we're confident this won't recur.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
